accepted.question_text: Let n be a positive integer, and let A1, ..., An be self-adjoint real n x n matrices with spectral norms bounded by 1 (that is, ||Ai|| <= 1 for every i). Does there exist a universal constant C > 0 such that one can always choose signs epsilon1, ..., epsilonn in {+1, -1} so that the operator norm of the signed sum is bounded by C*sqrt(n): ||sum_{i=1}^n epsiloni Ai|| <= C*sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 (Matrix Spencer). There exists a positive universal constant C such that, for all positive integers n, and all choices of n self-adjoint n×n real matrices A1, . . . , An satisfying, for all i ∈ [n], ∥Ai∥ ≤ 1 (where ∥ · ∥ denotes the spectral norm) the following holds min_{ε∈{±1}} ||sum_{i=1}^n εiAi|| ≤ C√n.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite group with |G| = n. Consider the n x n matrices A1, ..., An obtained from the regular representation of G. In this group-representation setting, is the Matrix Spencer bound true; namely, is there a universal constant C > 0 such that one can choose signs epsilon1, ..., epsilonn in {+1, -1} with ||sum_{i=1}^n epsiloni Ai|| <= C*sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 (Group Spencer). Let G be a finite group of size n. Conjecture 1 holds in the particular case in which A1, . . . , An are the n × n matrices corresponding to the regular representation of G.
In [BKMZ22] we prove Conjecture 2 for simple groups, but the general case is still open.

accepted.question_text: For a uniformly random 3-regular graph on n vertices, let E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) where A is the adjacency matrix, and call the graph globally synchronizing when all local minima of E are global minima corresponding to constant phase vectors theta_i = c. Is it true that a uniform random 3-regular graph is globally synchronizing with high probability as n -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3 (Globally Synchronizing Regular Graphs). A uniform random 3-regular graph is globally synchronizing with high probability (probability going to 1 as n → ∞).

accepted.question_text: Let A be an n x n random symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries independently equal to +1 with probability 1/2 + delta and -1 with probability 1/2 - delta, where delta >= (1 + epsilon)*sqrt((log n)/(2n)) for fixed epsilon > 0. Is A globally synchronizing with high probability as n -> infinity (in the sense that all local minima of E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) are global minima at constant phases)?
accepted.context_brief: Global synchrony with signed random edges

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4 (Global Synchrony with negative edges). Given any ε > 0, the n × n random matrix A with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries given by Aij = 1 with probability 1/2 + δ, and -1 with probability 1/2 - δ, with δ ≥ (1 + ε) sqrt(log n/(2n)), is globally synchronizing with high probability.
In this context, we are happy to report on two lines of progress: Conjecture 4 was answered by McRae in [McR25], following up on work of Rakoto Endor and Waldspurger [EW24].

accepted.question_text: For the Kuramoto-type global synchronization notion where a graph is globally synchronizing when all local minima of E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) are global minima at constant phases, is the following extremal statement true: for every epsilon > 0 there exists n and an n-vertex graph G with minimum degree at least (3/4 - epsilon)n that is not globally synchronizing?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5 (Density threshold for Global Synchrony). For any ε > 0, there exists n > 0 and a graph G on n nodes such that the minimum degree of G is at least (3/4 - ε)n and G is not globally synchronizing.

accepted.question_text: Let x1, ..., xn be independent Gaussian vectors in R^d with distribution N(0, Id/d). An origin-centered ellipsoid fit means there exists a positive semidefinite matrix S such that x_i^T S x_i = 1 for all i (equivalently, all points lie on the boundary of {x in R^d : x^T S x = 1}). Is there a sharp threshold at n/d^2 = 1/4 in the sense that for every epsilon > 0 one has P[ellipsoid fit exists] -> 1 when n/d^2 <= (1 - epsilon)/4 and P[ellipsoid fit exists] -> 0 when n/d^2 >= (1 + epsilon)/4 as d -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 (Ellipsoid fitting). Let n, d ≥ 1 and x1, · · · , xn ∼ N (0, Id/d). For any ε > 0: lim sup_{d→∞} n/d^2 ≤ (1-ε)/4 ⇒ lim_{d→∞} P[∃E an ellipsoid fit to (xi)^n_{i=1}] = 1, and lim inf_{d→∞} n/d^2 ≥ (1+ε)/4 ⇒ lim_{d→∞} P[∃E an ellipsoid fit to (xi)^n_{i=1}] = 0.

accepted.question_text: Consider multi-frequency group synchronization over SO(2) or over a finite group, with signal elements sampled uniformly from the group and observed through L frequency channels. Determine a scaling L = L_n such that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that reliably detects the signal as n -> infinity for all signal strengths lambda > lambda_comp,L with lambda_comp,L < 1.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Consider synchronization model over SO(2) or synchronization model over a finite group, where the signal x is sampled uniformly over group elements. Find a scaling L = Ln of number of frequencies such that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that can detect the signal reliably for all λ > λcomp,L for some λcomp,L < 1 as n → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Consider synchronization over SO(2) or over a finite group, with signal elements sampled uniformly over group elements, and fix a number of frequencies L that does not depend on n. In the computationally hard regime lambda in (lambda_stat, 1), does there exist a sub-exponential-time detection algorithm, specifically running in time exp(n^delta) for some delta < 1, that can reliably detect the signal as n -> infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Sub-exponential detection in hard synchronization regime

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. Consider synchronization model over SO(2) or synchronization model over a finite group, where the signal x is sampled uniformly over group elements. Fix number of frequencies L that does not depend on n. In the computationally hard regime, i.e., when λ ∈ (λstat, 1), does there exist a sub-exponential algorithm, i.e., an algorithm running in time exp n^δ for some δ < 1, that can detect the signal reliably as n → ∞?

accepted.question_text: Fix even tensor order r and integer level ell with n much larger than ell and ell >= r/2. Let M(lambda) be the matrix indexed by ell-subsets I, J of [n], with entries M(lambda)_{I,J} = lambda + Z_{IΔJ} when |IΔJ| = r and 0 otherwise, where Z_S are independent N(0,1) variables for |S| = r. Let lambda^natural_{r,ell} be the eigenvalue pop-out threshold of M(lambda). Is it true that for each fixed r, one has n^{r/4} * lambda^natural_{r,ell} -> 0 as ell -> infinity (after taking n -> infinity)?
accepted.context_brief: Kikuchi spectral threshold in Tensor PCA

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9 (Kikuchi Spectral Threshold). ... Let λ♮_{r,ℓ} denote the threshold at which eigenvalues "pop-out" of the spectrum of M(λ) ... For fixed r, we have n^{r/4} λ♮_{r,ℓ} → 0 as ℓ → ∞ (note that this is after one has taken n → ∞).

accepted.question_text: Define discrepancy of an n x n matrix A by disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity. For square matrices whose columns have unit l2 norm, does there exist a universal constant K such that disc(A) <= K for every such matrix A?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10 (K´omlos Conjecture). There exists a universal constant K such that, for all square matrices A whose columns have unit ℓ2 norm, disc(A) ≤ K.

accepted.question_text: Let disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity for A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}. What is the exact value of sup_{n in N} sup_{A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}} (1/sqrt(n)) * disc(A)?
accepted.context_brief: Worst-case normalized discrepancy of sign matrices

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 (How many deviations are needed afterall?). What is the value of the following quantity? sup_{n∈N} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} (1/√n) disc(A).

accepted.question_text: With discrepancy defined by disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity for A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}, is it true that limsup_{n->infinity} sup_{A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}} (1/sqrt(n)) * disc(A) > 1?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic lower bound above one for discrepancy

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12. Given the definitions above, we have lim sup_{n→∞} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} (1/√n) disc(A) > 1.

accepted.question_text: Let H_k be the 2^k x 2^k Hadamard matrix from Sylvester's construction. For odd k, is the discrepancy equal to sqrt(2) * sqrt(2^k), i.e., disc(H_k) = sqrt(2) * sqrt(2^k)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 13. Let Hk be the 2^k ×2^k Hadamard matrix obtained by the Sylvester construction (see above). For odd k, we have disc(Hk) = √2√(2^k).
Furthermore, Rares-Darius Buhai [Buh25] showed that Conjecture 13 is false by identifying a connection between discrepancy of Hk and a theory of non-linearity in Boolean Functions.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer n divisible by 4, does there exist an n x n Hadamard matrix (a matrix with entries in {+1,-1} and mutually orthogonal columns)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 14 (Hadamard Conjecture). For any positive n a multiple of 4, there exists an n×n Hadamard matrix.

accepted.question_text: Consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with interaction matrix J = beta W where W ~ GOE(n), with an arbitrary external field, and Glauber dynamics for sampling from the Gibbs measure on {+1,-1}^n. Does Glauber dynamics mix in polynomial time for all beta up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1?
accepted.context_brief: Fast mixing up to beta*=1 in SK model

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15. Consider the SK-model with an arbitrary external field. Does Glauber Dynamics fast mix (meaning in polynomial time) up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold β∗ = 1?
